response.overview: In the end, the two older gentlemen stood arm in arm on the stage, looked sunned into the city park half-round and waved, almost a little wistfully, to the 4000 cheering fans. It wasn't all that bad back then, in the 60s and 70s-"The Who" years, as Pete Townshend had recently asserted in frustration. Perhaps one concludes with age also his peace with the past and realizes that there were very well created works for the history book beyond the rock operetta "Tommy". "Behind Blue Eyes" for example: The mega-hit by Limp Bizkit is a who classic, which was presented this evening as fresh and driving as all the other big songs from 40 years of band memories.
response.title: The Who: Hamburg 6/18/2007
